children.text: Art has historically been inaccessible to the masses, for example during the Renaissance period rich landowners had the means to commission artists. Pockets of history shed glimpses into the presence and existence of an artisan class, especially prevalent among feudal societies. Slowly Europe transitioned away from feudalism and advanced towards capitalism pushing artisan class into extinction.

Technological advancements bring us to the 21st century where people no longer need the knowledge of specialized crafts, all of this culminating into the creation of the endangered crafts lists. The Red List of Endangered Crafts is an inventory of traditional crafts and trades practiced and are at risk of dying out in the succeeding generation.

According to the 2024 consumer report, Americans on average spend 4 hours and 30 minutes on their phone. I’d argue this increase in usage and dependence largely contributes to the surge in popularity of editing. The masses don’t have time nor the capital to invest in other non-digital forms of art.

Combined with rising costs affecting every form of entertainment are pushing people to look for more cheap forms of entertainment. Social media are free digital third spaces with Tiktok has about 1.9 billion active users and with the number of monthly active users on Instagram being over 2 billion users. Marking the first time the masses are able to access and utilize video editing as a form of art, but this specific expression aligns with it being profitable for companies.
